q: What makes the hyoid bone special compared with almost every other bone?
options: It is the only bone made of cartilage
It does not form a joint with any other bone – it hangs in muscles and ligaments
It is the only bone with no blood supply
It is fused to the mandible
why: The hyoid floats in the front of the neck. It is held only by muscles and ligaments (for example the stylohyoid ligament), not by a joint with another bone.

q: At which vertebral level does the hyoid bone lie at rest?
why: The hyoid sits at about the level of C3, between the chin and the thyroid cartilage.

q: Which group of muscles pulls the hyoid DOWN after swallowing?
why: The suprahyoid muscles lift the hyoid during swallowing; the infrahyoid (strap) muscles below it pull it back down.

q: In a post-mortem, the greater horn of the hyoid is broken. What does this classically suggest?
options: A fall onto the back of the head
why: Strong pressure from a hand around the throat can snap the thin greater horn – a classic forensic sign of strangulation.
